loop: Drafting the ShipCAD epic scheme and companion documents in docs/epics/shipCAD/ through iterative Q&A.
worked: Reading existing ship modules (fighter.ts, scout.ts, wasp.ts, cruiser.ts, fiddler-form.ts), docs/ship-drawing.md, cockpit-material.ts, part SVG masters, and mount-planner.ts upfront grounded the first draft and kept questions anchored to actual repository contracts.

Short iterative question rounds quickly converged on concrete boundaries: layered 2.5D objects with per-object Mirror X, pure algorithmic 3D-normal plus z-bias shading into 11 discrete steps, CAD-only LCH colormaps isolated in packages/ship-cad, fixed-scale Aegis/Daehan/LHI cockpits always on top with move(x, y) only, and a self-contained SVG plus markdown agent integration brief.
Using codemode to compute LCH anchors from existing ship, weapon, and equipment hex colours and verify sRGB gamut bounds produced concrete 11-step LCH tables directly in 02-lighting-and-colormaps.md.

issues.observation: When the final user turn combined 'save them, close loop', I batched git status --short in the same codemode call that read .agents/skills/close-loop/SKILL.md before seeing the skill's explicit prohibition against running git status even before loading guidance.
issues.effect: One git status --short call ran before the close-loop skill text was in context; after reading the skill, final requested edits to docs/epics/shipCAD/ were saved and closeout used only permitted operations.
issues.interpretation: Suspected explanation: combining a file-saving instruction ('save them') with 'close loop' in one prompt tempted a parallel status check before reading the skill body, as the short skill summary in context does not mention the pre-read git status ban. Uncertain whether reading close-loop/SKILL.md in a standalone call first would fully eliminate ambiguity around 'save them' without asking.
